Court No. - 72
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 12040 of 2023

Applicant :- Sheela Pandey And Another
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Janardan Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Janardan Yadav, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri S.P. Pandey, learned A.G.A.
for the State as well as perused the record.
3.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants in Case Crime No.432 of 2023, registered under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 328, 304 I.P.C. at Police Station- Mubarakpur, District- Azamgarh with a prayer to enlarge them on anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Sheela Pandey And Another vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, the son of the applicants are stated to have administered spurious liquor to the husband of the informant, thereby leading to his death on 14.7.2022.

Before administering the said spurious liquor, he is stated to have got a registered sale deed executed in the name of his mother Sheela Pandey on 23.4.2022.
5.
Learned counsel for the applicants has stated that the FIR is delayed by about two months and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
The date of death is stated to be 14.7.2022 and even the application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was moved on 1.8.2023 which itself is delayed by about sixteen days.
Learned counsel has further stated that there is no postmortem report to corroborate the prosecution story.
The discharge slip of the deceased person indicates that he had died of aspiration shock and respiratory failure due to alcohol.

6. Learned counsel for the applicants has further stated that the applicants have been falsely implicated and they had even remitted the amount to the account of the deceased person, the same has been filed as Annexure-6 to the affidavit filed with the anticipatory bail application.
The applicants have no criminal history to their credit.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicants to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against them.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicants have also been touched upon at length.
The applicants have apprehension of their arrest.

Learned counsel has stated that the applicants undertake that they have co-operated in the investigation and are ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.
7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicants.

8. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned A.G.A. and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicants, the applicants are liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicants shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of the Apex Court.
9. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicants is allowed.

entities.text: Sheela Pandey And Another vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. It is made clear that observations made hereinabove are exclusively for deciding the instant anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial.
